jobs.description: Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d)The Semiconductor Laboratory (HLL) of the Max Planck Society, located on the research campus in Garching near Munich, is a leading facility for the development of highly precise radiation sensors and detector systems. On approximately 1,400 m² of cleanroom space, HLL develops, fabricates and tests advanced semiconductor detectors for applications in X-ray astronomy, particle physics and materials research. With around 50 employees from different nationalities, HLL provides a highly international and interdisciplinary environment in which scientists, engineers and technology specialists work closely together across the entire development chain — from fundamental research and simulation to device design, fabrication and experimental characterization.To strengthen our activities in quantum sensing and advanced quantum-device technologies, and to provide scientific and technological support to our research, engineering and service teams, we are looking for a Scientist – Quantum Sensors & Qubit Technology (m/f/d) to join our team at the earliest possible date on a full-time basis (39 hours/week). Your responsibilities- Develop and optimize quantum sensor concepts based on qubit systems and quantum effects.- Perform advanced numerical simulations and modeling of qubit-based sensing systems, including relevant physical processes, noise sources and system-level performance.- Work closely with technology development, engineering and experimental teams to translate simulation results into practical implementations.- Analyze experimental data and use the results to refine physical models and sensor designs.- Contribute to scientific publications, technical documentation and intellectual property.Your profile- PhD in physics, electrical engineering, applied physics, quantum engineering or a related field.- Background in quantum sensing, qubit control and precision measurement.- Experience with numerical simulation, modeling and system design.- Analytical and problem-solving skills combined with a practical, technology-oriented mindset.- Strong motivation to work in close cooperation with technology, engineering and experimental teams.- Fluency in English; knowledge of German is an advantage.Advantageous experienceExperience in one or more of the following areas would be particularly valuable:- Cleanroom / semiconductor / microfabrication experience- Familiarity with Python, MATLAB, COMSOL or equivalent - MEMS/NEMS or integrated sensor technologies- Precision measurement and low-noise instrumentation- Experience bridging qubit physics, device design and fabrication technologyWhat we offer- International environment, diverse responsibilities and a high degree of autonomy: Flat hierarchies and a collaborative, agile team within an internationally renowned research institution. You will work closely with scientists, engineers and technology specialists across disciplines and have the opportunity to shape the development of innovative quantum-sensing technologies.- Advantages of the public sector: Remuneration according to the German public service pay scale TVöD (Bund), depending on qualifications and experience; occupational pension scheme (VBL); 30 days of annual leave (31 days as of 2027), plus additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve. jobs.description: Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d) – Experimental Cancer NeuroscienceFull- or part-time | temporary (36 months) | Klinik und Poliklinik für ChirurgieWe are seeking an exceptional and highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our internationally active research group at the interface of cancer biology, neuroscience and tumor immunology.Our group investigates how the nervous system shapes tumor initiation, progression, invasion, metastasis and cancer-associated symptoms, with a particular focus on pancreatic cancer and cancer neuroscience. We combine mechanistic cancer biology with neuroscience, immunology, advanced in vivo models, spatial and single-cell technologies, functional imaging and translational human studies.Our ambition is clear: to define and lead emerging concepts in cancer neuroscience rather than merely follow them.The laboratory operates in a highly competitive and well-funded environment with support from, among others, the European Research Council (ERC), Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG), Deutsche Krebshilfe and Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung, and is embedded in a strong national and international network in cancer neuroscience.Your responsibilities:The successful candidate will take a central scientific role in our experimental program and will contribute to the conception, execution and development of ambitious projects addressing neural–tumor–immune interactions.Depending on expertise, projects may include:- mechanistic studies of neuron–cancer and neuro–immune interactions- jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day As an Industrial Cybersecurity Expert (f/m/d) you will help strengthen cybersecurity across manufacturing OT (Operational Technologies) environments. You will work in a global setting, collaborating daily with colleagues from multiple countries. Using your IT/OT security expertise, you will support, consult, and guide factory teams on cybersecurity topics. You will help shape secure manufacturing principles and contribute to the development of secure IT and OT infrastructures. This will play a key role in addressing cybersecurity needs across manufacturing environments.How You’ll Make an Impact * Define secure manufacturing principles and support the development of secure manufacturing IT and OT infrastructure* Translate IT/OT governance policies and controls into practical implementation measures for manufacturing environments* Define cybersecurity requirements and demands from factories and ensure they are addressed effectively* Specify and maintain configuration and hardening guidelines for our products, third-party components, and manufacturing equipment* Collaborate with functions such as GT ICS, SE CYS/IT, and Digitalization GPO to help secure manufacturing, production, and product development environments, and provide guidance and documentation support throughout development and engineering processes.What You Bring* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in IT Security, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering with a focus on IT Security, or similar experience in IT and OT environments* Many years of experience in Industrial Cybersecurity / IT Security* Knowledge of manufacturing infrastructure and IT/OT security technologies and concepts, including IIoT, Connected Factory environments, OT hardware, and sensors* Experience with risk-based approaches such as threat and risk analysis, as well as incident and vulnerability handling* Understanding of international or national IT/OT security standards, regulations, and related legal considerations* Very good, user-focused communication skills both in German and English, a value- and solution-driven mindset, and experience in stakeholder managementAbout the TeamOur Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.  Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences.
